title: Saffron Platform - Console walkthrough (usage analytics & per-route cost breakdown)
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Console focusing on per-route usage and cost attribution for FinOps. Demoed per-route dashboards, live filters, cost waterfall, and Optimize recommendations. Customer requested tailored pricing and a short pilot with perf targets and security docs.
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — this is Maya from Redwood, I'll kick us off. Uh quick check on audio?
00:18 Liam O'Connor: Audio's good here, thanks.
00:38 Maya Chen: Great. Today's agenda: quick intro, then Ethan will jump into the console to show usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdowns, and finish with Optimize suggestions and next steps.
01:05 Ethan Park: Okay jumping in — I'm sharing my screen, should show the Console home with the routes list, top-level usage chart, and left nav. Let me know if you can't see.
01:25 Priya Mehta: Seeing it. Can you make the chart a little bigger?
01:38 Ethan Park: Yep. So top-left is token-level usage over time, you can change granularity, and here we have an example filter by route group, environment, and model family.
02:12 Jules Rivera: That route group view is what we care about — we have about 120 routes in prod, need to attribute costs to product teams.
02:40 Ethan Park: Totally. We built per-route dashboards for exactly that: each route has latency distribution, token split, cost per 1k tokens, and a waterfall showing where spend comes from — model compute, quantization overhead, and KV cache misses.
03:10 Priya Mehta: KV cache misses? We keep hearing K-V cash on threads, sorry if I'm butchering acronyms.
03:25 Ethan Park: Totally — KV cache (sometimes transcribed as K-V cash) — it's the prefix cache; misses show up in extra decode tokens and increase per-request cost. In the console the waterfall shows percent of cost from decode tokens vs cache fetch etc.
03:50 Maya Chen: Quick interjection: on the left there's a Cost Insights tab that flips the view from usage to cost. We can also group by team or tag if you push metadata in the request.
04:20 Liam O'Connor: We tag routes by product area but not consistently. How hard is it to retro-tag?
04:40 Ethan Park: There's an ingestion mapping you can run; for the pilot we often help run a backfill to populate route tags from your internal route registry.
05:05 Priya Mehta: Show us an example route — say the customer-support-chat route — what's the breakdown look like?
05:30 Ethan Park: Opening the route: you can see requests per minute, p50/p95 latency, token histogram. Scrolling to Cost Breakdown: model compute is 72%, embedding calls (we sometimes see them for rerank) 8%, KV cache misses 12%, and batching inefficiency 8%.
06:10 Jules Rivera: Batching inefficiency meaning small batch sizes?
06:22 Ethan Park: Right — small bursts increase per-token overhead. Our Optimize tab will suggest batch sizes and pooling config.
06:45 Maya Chen: Also note you can pin a route to use a cheaper quantized variant in non-critical paths — that shows a simulated cost delta right there.
07:18 Liam O'Connor: The simulation — is that based on actual sampled requests or a model?
07:32 Ethan Park: It's sampled traffic plus our performance profiles for each model/quantization combo. We try to be conservative; you can run a live canary to validate.
08:05 Priya Mehta: Can we see cross-team dashboards? Priya wants to map costs back to teams.
08:20 Ethan Park: Sure — switch to Team view, group by tag, show top 5 routes contributing to FinOps team cost. Example: three routes make up 64% of spend. You can drill into date ranges, specific model versions, and see per-token latency and cost.
09:00 Priya Mehta: Can you export that as CSV for internal chargeback?
09:10 Ethan Park: Yes, Export CSV or connect to BigQuery via our export connector — some customers pipe daily aggregates to their data warehouse.
09:30 Jules Rivera: Security — how granular are the logs? We need audit trails for model versions and who changed routing policies.
09:50 Sofia Alvarez: We keep audit logs for rollouts, config changes, model pinning. For Private/VPC deployments logs can be forwarded to your SIEM; we support SAML/SSO (sometimes transcribed as Sam-el), RBAC roles, and KMS integrations.
10:20 Liam O'Connor: Good. For our compliance team we'll need SOC2 docs — can you share?
10:35 Maya Chen: Absolutely, we'll attach the security pack.
11:00 Ethan Park: Back to Optimize — here's a recommendation card: increase target batch size from 8 to 24 for your long-answer routes, and enable prefix caching on the support-chat route; estimated cost reduction ~28% with minimal p95 impact.
11:38 Priya Mehta: 28% is attractive. Any downside on latency?
11:48 Ethan Park: Small p50 bump for tail requests if batching introduces a tiny queue; but we have latency SLO knobs — you can set max queue wait and we auto-fallback to a lower-latency variant if SLO is violated.
12:20 Liam O'Connor: How does Dedicated capacity show up in the console?
12:35 Maya Chen: We display dedicated pools as a separate region in routing, with SLA metrics. You can assign routes to Dedicated pool, and the cost model is commit-based — the console will show effective unit cost relative to hosted.
13:05 Jules Rivera: For our initial pilot we want predictable latency, so Dedicated sounds right. What's the typical lead time?
13:20 Maya Chen: Depends on size; small pools can be provisioned in weeks, larger in a month or so. We'll include options in the pricing packet.
13:45 Priya Mehta: Let's talk pilot success metrics: Priya lists 99th percentile latency under 450ms for support-chat and cost under $X per 1k tokens — can we run benchmarks?
14:05 Ethan Park: Yes — we can run a benchmark harness against a private endpoint or mock traffic via a test route. We also provide a perf spreadsheet to share.
14:40 Liam O'Connor: Are there limits on retention for usage data? Compliance might ask to limit retention.
14:55 Sofia Alvarez: Console defaults to 90 days but can be reduced; for Private we can set retention per contract.
15:20 Maya Chen: Quick demo of the Live Trace view — you can see a sample request trace with step timings: request received, model decode, KV hit/miss, post-processing.
16:05 Priya Mehta: Can we annotate traces for bad outputs? I.e., tie quality regressions to a model rollout?
16:22 Ethan Park: Yes. We have a quality monitor where you can tag prompts and track regressions; when a rollout coincides with score drops we alert and can auto-rollback.
17:05 Jules Rivera: Any integrations with SLO tooling like Prometheus?
17:18 Sofia Alvarez: We export metrics to Prometheus and Datadog; traces can be linked to your tracing system.
17:45 Maya Chen: Okay I'll pause demo — any questions on what you saw so far?
18:00 Priya Mehta: One more on cost allocation — can cost be backdated once we apply tagging?
18:20 Ethan Park: We can backfill tags for usage aggregates but not reconstruct exact historical per-request tag state in all cases; we advise starting tagging before pilot but can help with a best-effort backfill that usually covers most of the last 30-90 days.
19:00 Liam O'Connor: For the pricing piece — will you send a tailored spreadsheet with hosted vs dedicated scenarios?
19:12 Maya Chen: Yes, next steps we'll send pricing + a recommended pilot scope and a proposed timeline.
19:30 Priya Mehta: Also need SOC2 docs, and a slot for a security deep-dive with our security team.
19:45 Maya Chen: We'll schedule that; Ethan will lead the deep dive.
20:05 Jules Rivera: A few small transcription notes — sometimes model names come out wrong in transcripts.
20:20 Maya Chen: [laughter] yes our transcripts aren't perfect.
20:35 Ethan Park: Quick note on competitors you asked about: we compared unit cost and feature parity with Anthropic and Cohere on the perf spreadsheet; Redwood's unique is the per-route Optimize recommendations.
21:00 Priya Mehta: That feature is useful.
21:12 Liam O'Connor: Anything else on the console export / API?
21:25 Ethan Park: API endpoints allow querying route-level aggregates, create filters, and trigger rollouts. We'll share API docs.
22:00 Maya Chen: Recap and next steps in a sec — anything else?
22:12 Priya Mehta: No, that's it.
22:20 Maya Chen: Great thanks everyone — we'll follow up with pricing, SOC2 pack, perf spreadsheet, and a proposed pilot schedule.
22:35 Ethan Park: I'll also kick off a proposed benchmark and share steps to instrument tagging.
22:50 Liam O'Connor: Thanks all.
23:05 [meeting ends]

Note: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., K-V cash for KV cache, Sam-el for SAML); deck and perf spreadsheet referenced during demo.
